name: project-mm241-live-migration
description: "MM-241 live bsky.social migration round-trip — leg status, the three walls leg (b) hit, and reference-PDS interop lessons"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: e14e454c-c592-4d1c-a1a3-c4845a1bea84
---

MM-241 = validate a live bsky.social migration round trip with the wallet.

**Status (2026-07-12):** leg (r) (sim rehearsal staging→production) PASSED; **leg (b) (on-device bsky.social → ezpds-staging) PASSED**; **Custos→Custos live hop (staging → production/obsign.org) PASSED same day, zero new walls** — lossless (same rev both sides), staging cleanly deactivated. Test account `malpercio-obsign.bsky.social` / `did:plc:u7j7xdhvkwx3xlf6xjkbpdn7` now lives on PRODUCTION, device key still rotationKeys[0] through three PLC ops. Remaining: the return leg to bsky.social (Custos source → reference destination; watch bsky's signup gates on migration-mode createAccount). Pre-flight gotcha that cost time: migrated accounts have NO password (MM-306) and the staging account's email was typo'd (MM-308 normalization, MM-309 operator repair ops) — unblocked via requestPasswordReset + token fished from Railway logs (log-only email sender).

Leg (b) took three fixes, each moving the failure one pipeline step (pattern: expect a NEW wall per step when first exercising a reference-PDS seam Custos-to-Custos testing masked):
1. **MM-301** — claim flow cached the W3C DID doc (empty rotationKeys) → migrate button hidden; fix = canonical `GET /{did}/data` fetch everywhere + home-screen cache self-heal (`refresh_did_doc`).
2. **MM-302** — bsky refuses `getServiceAuth(lxm=com.atproto.server.createAccount)` below the *privileged* tier; OAuth `transition:generic` = plain-app-password tier. Fix = outbound-migration source login is a password `createSession` full session (like the claim flow, ADR-0021). Both wallet source logins are now password-based; only the create flow uses OAuth.
3. **MM-304** — Custos `verify_service_auth_jwt` was ES256/P-256-only, but bsky signs service-auth JWTs with the account's secp256k1 `#atproto` key (ES256K). Fix = crypto `verify_did_key_signature` (dual-curve, per-curve low-S) + alg↔key-curve binding in jwt.rs.

**Recurring interop lesson:** bsky signs *everything* (PLC ops, service-auth JWTs) with secp256k1 (`zQ3s…`); any Custos verifier of foreign-account signatures must dispatch both curves. Custos's `require_rpc` is laxer than the reference about which lxm an unprivileged token can mint — [[project-custos-strictness-parity]] / MM-292 family; that laxness masks walls until a bsky source is used.

**Loose ends:** the `.bsky.social` handle is now dangling (bsky no longer actively hosts the account → handle-invalid on the network until a served-domain handle or a migration back). Test-account password `JDZw3if3l!rox1` appears in transcripts — rotate it.

content.text:
Everything's recorded. Where the return leg stands:

**The verdict is clean: our side is provably correct, bsky's side is rejecting.** Your production-minted token verified perfectly against an atproto-conformant verifier resolving the DID's *current* key from plc.directory — signature, curve, claims, expiry, everything. bsky's `InvalidToken` means they're checking against a stale view of your DID (two PLC ops in one day is exactly the scenario that outruns a lazy cache) — or masking an inbound-migration policy refusal. Their auth-gated `reserveSigningKey` and the phone-verification wall suggest the entryway was never made hospitable to walk-ins, which is, notably, *the thesis of this whole product expressed as an error code*.

The investigation paid for itself twice over, though — chasing their bug found **ours**: [MM-310](https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-310/did-doc-cache-never-refreshes-custos-verifies-inbound-migrations) (High). Custos's `resolve_did_document` is cache-first with no refresh path, `refreshIdentity` is demonstrably a no-op (I called it against production; the fossil doc came straight back), and since the migration verifier uses that same resolution, **an account migrating back to a Custos that had ever seen it before would be rejected exactly the way bsky rejected us.** Both hops tonight succeeded only because the destinations were cache-cold. The ticket has the reference-parity fix spec (force-refresh path, real `refreshIdentity`, retry-once-on-signature-failure in the verifier).

The plan on [MM-241](https://linear.app/atbb/issue/MM-241): retry the authenticated probe in ~24h — if it's their cache TTL, it heals itself and the return leg is back on. If it's still walled, the return-leg validation moves to a **self-hosted reference PDS** as destination, which proves every seam that's ours to prove (a reference-implementation verifier accepting our ES256 token, reference `importRepo`/blob intake), and bsky.social's posture gets recorded as a finding rather than a failure.

Meanwhile the identity sits happily on production — keys sovereign through three PLC ops, two live hops verified. Whenever you pick this back up: MM-310 is the one to land first if the next move is any migration *into* a warm Custos; the 24h bsky retry is a single curl away. Solid night's work.

2	
3	**Status: LEGS (a) AND (r) EXECUTED (both pass — see the execution record); legs (b)–(d)
4	pending.** Leg (r) additionally flushed out and validated fixes for five defects
5	(MM-295/297/298/299 server-side, MM-300 wallet-side) before any leg touched the real
6	identity.
7	This document is both the checklist for the live bsky.social migration round trip and, after
8	execution, the permanent record of the run. A human operator executes or supervises every
9	leg: the run touches the real plc.directory, the real bsky.social, and permanent `did:plc`
10	state.
11	
12	- Ticket: [MM-241](https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-241) (the canonical MM-207 e2e; the
13	  one unvalidated leg of the migration epic)
14	- Design: [ADR-0002](../architecture/decisions/0002-wallet-authorized-account-migration.md),
15	  design plan [v0.1 operational proof](../archive/design-plans/2026-07-07-v01-operational-proof.md)
16	  (op-proof.AC4)
17	- Tooling: the Obsign wallet (all legs), `curl` + `jq` for the plc.directory audit and
18	  resolution checks. The interop CLI's `migrate perform`/`migrate verify`
19	  ([`tools/interop`](../../tools/interop/README.md)) is the **fallback driver only** — see
20	  "Fallback: interop-driven variant" at the end.
21	
22	## Revision note (2026-07-11)
23	
24	The original runbook assumed leg (a) was a full inbound migration (repoint to staging +
25	deactivate on bsky) and drove legs (b)/(c) with the interop CLI against an interop-managed
26	identity. Leg (a) as shipped is **claim-only** (the phased custody-first design): the wallet
27	key was inserted at `rotationKeys[0]` and the account stayed on bsky.social. Consequently
28	the identity's rotation key lives in the phone's Secure Enclave, not in
29	`tools/interop/.state/state.json`, and the remaining legs are **wallet-driven end to end**.
30	This is a *stronger* proof than the original plan: every hop's PLC op is self-signed by the
31	Secure-Enclave-held key via the wallet's outbound-migration flow — the source PDS never
32	signs, and no email token is needed after leg (a).
33	
34	## The round trip
35	
36	| Leg | From → To | Driver | What it proves |
37	|---|---|---|---|
38	| (a) Claim | custody: bsky.social PDS → wallet | Obsign wallet claim flow ("Bring an identity") | **DONE 2026-07-11.** PDS-signed insertion path: bsky.social's email-tokened `signPlcOperation` inserted the wallet's device key as `rotationKeys[0]` |
39	| (r) Rehearsal *(optional but recommended)* | staging → production, **throwaway identity** | Obsign wallet in the iOS simulator | The full outbound orchestrator (service auth, claim-code account creation, repo/blob/prefs transfer, review guard, self-signed op, activate/deactivate) with zero risk to the real identity |
40	| (b) Outbound | bsky.social → ezpds staging | Obsign wallet outbound flow, on device | **The differentiator**: the Secure-Enclave rotation key self-signs the PLC op; bsky.social never signs and cannot veto |
41	| (c) Hop | ezpds staging → ezpds production | Obsign wallet outbound flow, on device | Custos→Custos migration; custody unchanged across a second hop |
42	| (d) Return | ezpds production → ezpds staging | Obsign wallet outbound flow, on device | Round-trip closure; nothing about the identity degraded |
43	
44	Deployments: staging `https://ezpds-staging.up.railway.app`, production
45	`https://obsign.org`.
46	
47	## Required pass conditions — checked after EVERY leg
48	
49	A leg is **not passed** because "the flow completed". Both checks below must be recorded per
50	leg (these are MM-241's acceptance criteria):
51	
52	**1. plc.directory audit log shows the correct new entry for the hop.**
53	
54	```sh
55	DID="did:plc:u7j7xdhvkwx3xlf6xjkbpdn7"   # the migrating identity
56	curl -s "https://plc.directory/$DID/log/audit" | jq '.[-1] | {createdAt, nullified, operation: {rotationKeys: .operation.rotationKeys, pds: .operation.services.atproto_pds.endpoint}}'
57	```
58	
59	Expected per leg (`WALLET_KEY` = `did:key:REDACTED`):
60	- after (a): **recorded — see execution record.** `rotationKeys[0]` = `WALLET_KEY`; services
61	  unchanged (claim-only); entry not nullified.
62	- after (b): `atproto_pds.endpoint` = staging URL; `rotationKeys[0]` still = `WALLET_KEY`
63	  (the op was **self-signed by it** — bsky's old `zQ3…` keys are replaced by
64	  `WALLET_KEY` + staging's recommended keys); not nullified.
65	- after (c): `atproto_pds.endpoint` = production URL; `rotationKeys[0]` still = `WALLET_KEY`.
66	- after (d): `atproto_pds.endpoint` = staging URL; `rotationKeys[0]` still = `WALLET_KEY`.
67	
68	**2. Handle, DID document, and repo all resolve correctly against the new host.**
69	
70	```sh
71	HANDLE="<the account handle>"
72	NEW_PDS="https://ezpds-staging.up.railway.app"   # the leg's destination
73	
74	# Handle → DID (on the new host)
75	curl -s "$NEW_PDS/xrpc/com.atproto.identity.resolveHandle?handle=$HANDLE" | jq .
76	
77	# DID document points at the new host
78	curl -s "https://plc.directory/$DID" | jq '.service[] | select(.id=="#atproto_pds").serviceEndpoint'
79	
80	# Repo serveable from the new host
81	curl -s "$NEW_PDS/xrpc/com.atproto.sync.getLatestCommit?did=$DID" | jq .
82	```
83	
84	The interop CLI's `migrate verify` does **not** apply to the wallet-custody identity (it is
85	not interop-managed) — use the raw curls above.
86	
87	**If a leg fails:** record the failure below, file a bug (its own Linear issue, linked to
88	MM-241), and **stop the run**. Do not paper over a failed check to reach the next leg.
89	Expect this: the outbound flow has never run against real bsky.social, and leg (a) needed
90	six fixes to survive first contact (see execution record).
91	
92	## Preconditions
93	
94	- [ ] Both ezpds deployments healthy:
95	      `curl -s https://ezpds-staging.up.railway.app/xrpc/_health` and the production
96	      equivalent return 200. Staging sleeps when idle — hit it once and wait for wake.
97	- [ ] Wallet build ≥ `c7373fc3` (carries the six leg-(a) fixes: MM-288/289/290/291/293/294)
98	      installed **on the physical device** — legs (b)–(d) must run on the phone, because the
99	      self-signing key is its Secure Enclave key. The simulator is only valid for leg (r).
100	- [ ] Leg (a) complete: `WALLET_KEY` at `rotationKeys[0]` of the migrating DID (verify with

103	- [ ] **Claim codes minted for every destination** — staging for legs (r-source is created

107	- [ ] The bsky.social test account credentials at hand (leg (b)'s source OAuth login).
108	      No email token is needed for legs (b)–(d) — the identity leg is self-signed.

112	
113	## Rollback notes for the live account
114	
115	There is no "undo" for a PLC op — rollback means **executing the reverse migration**, which

input.title: Config enum values are case-sensitive — EZPDS_EMAIL_PROVIDER=SMTP crashes startup
input.description:
## Problem

`EZPDS_EMAIL_PROVIDER=SMTP` (all-caps) fails config validation and aborts startup — the provider match in `crates/pds/src/email.rs` (`sender_from_config`) accepts only the exact lowercase strings `"log"` / `"smtp"`. Env-var values are conventionally written in caps, so this is an easy operator trap: the service crash-loops on deploy over pure letter case.

## Fix

- Normalize enum-valued config strings case-insensitively (`value.trim().to_ascii_lowercase()`) before matching. Audit ALL enum-valued config keys, not just email provider — at minimum: `email.provider`, `[telemetry] log_format` (`"json"`), and any boolean-ish envs parsed by string match.
- Keep unknown values a hard, *descriptive* config error (naming the accepted values) — the crash-on-invalid posture is right; the case-sensitivity is not.
- Tests: uppercase/mixed-case values accepted for each enum key; genuinely unknown value still fails with the enumerated-options message.

Observed live while configuring SMTP on a deployment (2026-07-12, MM-241 aftermath).

During the create flow's first OAuth (the `authenticating` step after handle registration), the in-app authorize page:
1. **Doesn't prefill the username** — even though the wallet literally just registered the handle two screens earlier.
2. **iOS auto-capitalizes the first letter** of the identifier, and the login then fails — annoying and mysterious to a user (the failure gives no hint that case was the problem).

## Root causes

1. The `login_hint` plumbing **already exists end-to-end and is simply not fed**: the authorize template renders `login_hint` into the identifier field (`oauth_templates.rs` — `value="{login_hint}"`, `autocomplete="username"`), `CustosClient::par()` forwards a `login_hint`, and `oauth::prepare_oauth_flow` accepts one — but the frontend's `startOAuthFlow` never supplies the handle. Wallet fix: pass the just-registered handle (create flow has it in state) through `startOAuthFlow` → `prepare_oauth_flow`.
2. The authorize page's identifier `<input>` sets no `autocapitalize`/`autocorrect`/`spellcheck` attributes → iOS capitalizes. Server fix (template): `autocapitalize="none" autocorrect="off" spellcheck="false"`.
3. Defense in depth: the authorize login (and `createSession`) should match identifiers **case-insensitively** — handles are stored lowercase, so `Malpercio.…` fails byte-equality today. Lowercase the identifier before handle resolution (emails: MM-308's normalization covers that side).

Three small fixes, two surfaces (wallet + Custos template/login); together they make the first-login step feel intentional instead of hostile.

input.title: Migration source login prefills the DID instead of the handle
input.description:
## Problem (user-observed, on device, MM-241 legs (b)/(c))

The outbound-migration source-login screen prefills the identifier field with the **DID** (`did:plc:…`) rather than the handle — technically valid (createSession accepts DIDs) but strange as a user: you expect to see your name, not your key.

## Root cause pointer

`MigrationSourceAuthScreen` prefills from its `handle` prop and its comment says handle is intended ("Prefill the login identifier with the handle, then let the user edit it to a DID or email…"). So the *supplier* hands it a DID: either `prepare_migration`'s `PreparedMigration.handle` falls back to the DID (likely when the cached DID doc lacks a usable `alsoKnownAs` — related to the MM-300/301 cache-shape history), or the `+page.svelte` wiring passes `identity.did`. Trace which and fix at the source; fall back to the DID only when no handle is known.

Cheap fix; worth batching with the create-flow OAuth UX ticket (login_hint/autocapitalize) as one wallet-polish PR.

All three filed, with root causes pinned from the code:

- **[MM-313](https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-313/config-enum-values-are-case-sensitive-ezpds-email-providersmtp-crashes)** (Medium) — `EZPDS_EMAIL_PROVIDER=SMTP` crashes startup; the provider match is exact-lowercase. Fix is case-insensitive normalization across *all* enum-valued config keys (the ticket flags `log_format` etc. for the audit), while keeping unknown values a hard, descriptive error.
- **[MM-314](https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-314/create-flow-oauth-login-ux-no-username-autofill-login-hint-never)** (Medium) — the fun finding: the `login_hint` plumbing already exists end-to-end (authorize template renders it into the field, `par()` forwards it, `prepare_oauth_flow` accepts it) — the frontend just never passes the handle it registered two screens earlier. Plus the missing `autocapitalize="none"/autocorrect="off"` on the authorize page's input, plus case-insensitive identifier matching as defense in depth (your capitalized-first-letter failure is byte-equality against lowercase-stored handles — MM-308's cousin).
- **[MM-315](https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-315/migration-source-login-prefills-the-did-instead-of-the-handle)** (Low) — the source-auth screen *intends* to prefill the handle (its own comment says so); something upstream hands it the DID instead, likely `PreparedMigration.handle` falling back when the cached doc lacked `alsoKnownAs`. Noted as a natural batch with MM-314 in one wallet-polish PR.

Meanwhile the staging monitor is still polling — CI was mid-run when we last looked, and Railway builds the image after the green check, so the MM-310 deploy flipping the fossil doc to production's key is probably 5–15 minutes out. I'll report the moment it flips, and then leg (d) is go.

input.title: importRepo's first-write-wins guard blocks return migration into a prior residency — MM-241 leg (d) blocker
input.description:
## Found by

MM-241 **leg (d)** (production → staging, the round-trip closer), on device, 2026-07-12: fails at transfer-repo with `REPO_TRANSFER_FAILED`. One step past MM-310's fix (the warm-cache `createAccount` verified fine — that fix is confirmed live).

## Root cause

Two individually-correct designs interact badly:

- **MM-299** made migration-mode `createAccount` resumable: an existing **deactivated** account for the DID re-issues a session instead of 409ing. Leg (d) resumed the leg (b) staging account.
- **`import_repo`** is first-write-wins (`routes/import_repo.rs`): `if write_state.repo_root_cid.is_some()` → `409 Conflict "account already has a repo"` — written for the mid-flight-retry picture (root absent, or import already complete), protecting against a retried/racing call silently overwriting.

Nobody considered a **completed prior residency**: the resumed account still carries leg (b)'s full repo root, so the return migration's import 409s deterministically. Any migrate-away-and-return round trip hits this; the reference ecosystem supports round trips, so this is also a parity gap.

## State note (leg (d) attempt is cleanly retryable)

The resume consumed nothing (no claim code) and changed nothing; staging's account remains deactivated at leg (b)'s root/rev `3mqdcm57v4u22`. In this specific run the incoming repo is **byte-identical** (same rev — no writes happened on production), which suggests the fix's first tier below already unblocks leg (d).

## Fix design

Server (`import_repo`), two tiers:
1. **Idempotent same-root import**: if the parsed CAR's root == the existing `repo_root_cid`, return 200 without rewriting — a retried import (and this leg-(d) case) is a no-op success.
2. **Replace-on-deactivated with optimistic concurrency**: allow a *different* root to replace the existing one while the account is deactivated, making the atomic commit a compare-and-swap against the root observed at precondition time (`UPDATE … WHERE repo_root_cid IS <observed-old-root>`), so the anti-race property the first-write-wins guard provided is preserved (a concurrent import with a different base loses loudly, nothing is silently clobbered). The deactivated state + the service-auth-derived session is the authorization — same trust chain that authorized the resume.
   - Housekeeping: superseded blocks/`block_owners` rows from the old root become unreferenced → existing GC reconciliation covers them; confirm `blob_owners` grace behavior for blobs no longer referenced by the new root.

Wallet (optional hardening, separate ticket if preferred): `transfer_repo_impl` could treat a dest whose `checkAccountStatus` already reconciles with the source head as import-complete and skip — the orchestrator already has `import_reconciles` machinery.

Tests: same-root reimport 200 no-op (replaces the current `reimport_over_existing_repo_returns_409` expectation); different-root replace succeeds while deactivated; CAS loser errors loudly; active account still refused.

Sequence: land → staging auto-deploy → retry leg (d) with the same (unconsumed) claim code and wallet build.

<issue id="10c8aa2a-f2fe-433f-9ba4-fed81b554e7a" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-241/validate-live-bskysocial-migration-round-trip-canonical-mm-207-e2e">MM-241</issue> **leg (d)** (production → staging, the round-trip closer), on device, 2026-07-12: fails at transfer-repo with `REPO_TRANSFER_FAILED`. One step past <issue id="f029449e-4a4d-4fd1-ab17-955b0e40a156" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-310/did-doc-cache-never-refreshes-custos-verifies-inbound-migrations">MM-310</issue>'s fix (the warm-cache `createAccount` verified fine — that fix is confirmed live).

## Root cause

Two individually-correct designs interact badly:

* <issue id="91456924-d043-4164-baa8-112e1ff1e865" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-299/migration-mode-createaccount-is-not-resumable-a-mid-flight-failure">MM-299</issue> made migration-mode `createAccount` resumable: an existing **deactivated** account for the DID re-issues a session instead of 409ing. Leg (d) resumed the leg (b) staging account.
* `import_repo` is first-write-wins (`routes/import_repo.rs`): `if write_state.repo_root_cid.is_some()` → `409 Conflict "account already has a repo"` — written for the mid-flight-retry picture (root absent, or import already complete), protecting against a retried/racing call silently overwriting.

Nobody considered a **completed prior residency**: the resumed account still carries leg (b)'s full repo root, so the return migration's import 409s deterministically. Any migrate-away-and-return round trip hits this; the reference ecosystem supports round trips, so this is also a parity gap.

## State note (leg (d) attempt is cleanly retryable)

The resume consumed nothing (no claim code) and changed nothing; staging's account remains deactivated at leg (b)'s root/rev `3mqdcm57v4u22`. In this specific run the incoming repo is **byte-identical** (same rev — no writes happened on production), which suggests the fix's first tier below already unblocks leg (d).

## Fix design

Server (`import_repo`), two tiers:

1. **Idempotent same-root import**: if the parsed CAR's root == the existing `repo_root_cid`, return 200 without rewriting — a retried import (and this leg-(d) case) is a no-op success.
2. **Replace-on-deactivated with optimistic concurrency**: allow a *different* root to replace the existing one while the account is deactivated, making the atomic commit a compare-and-swap against the root observed at precondition time (`UPDATE … WHERE repo_root_cid IS <observed-old-root>`), so the anti-race property the first-write-wins guard provided is preserved (a concurrent import with a different base loses loudly, nothing is silently clobbered). The deactivated state + the service-auth-derived session is the authorization — same trust chain that authorized the resume.
   * Housekeeping: superseded blocks/`block_owners` rows from the old root become unreferenced → existing GC reconciliation covers them; confirm `blob_owners` grace behavior for blobs no longer referenced by the new root.

Wallet (optional hardening, separate ticket if preferred): `transfer_repo_impl` could treat a dest whose `checkAccountStatus` already reconciles with the source head as import-complete and skip — the orchestrator already has `import_reconciles` machinery.

Tests: same-root reimport 200 no-op (replaces the current `reimport_over_existing_repo_returns_409` expectation); different-root replace succeeds while deactivated; CAS loser errors loudly; active account still refused.

MM-241 = validate a live bsky.social migration round trip with the wallet.

**Status (2026-07-12):** leg (r) (sim rehearsal staging→production) PASSED; **leg (b) (on-device bsky.social → ezpds-staging) PASSED**; **Custos→Custos live hop (staging → production/obsign.org) PASSED same day, zero new walls** — lossless (same rev both sides), staging cleanly deactivated. Test account `malpercio-obsign.bsky.social` / `did:plc:u7j7xdhvkwx3xlf6xjkbpdn7` now lives on PRODUCTION, device key still rotationKeys[0] through three PLC ops. **Leg letters per the runbook** (`docs/validation/2026-07-07-mm-241-live-migration.md` — the permanent record; operator handle "mal"): (a) claim ✓, (r) sim rehearsal ✓, (b) bsky→staging ✓, (c) staging→production ✓ — **remaining: leg (d) = production → STAGING** (round-trip closure; NOT a return to bsky). **Leg (d) is hard-blocked by MM-310**: staging cached this DID's doc as leg (b)'s destination, and `resolve_did_document` is cache-first/no-refresh (`refreshIdentity` is a no-op), so leg (d)'s inbound createAccount would verify production's token against the fossil doc → InvalidToken deterministically. Sequence: land MM-310 → staging deploy → leg (d). Runbook's execution-record table still needs legs (b)/(c) rows appended (evidence in MM-241 comments).

Extra-curricular bsky-return probing (not a required leg): bsky's entryway auth-gates reserveSigningKey, phone-gates createAccount, and rejected a PROVABLY VALID production ES256 service token (verified perfect against a local Custos impersonating did:web:bsky.social) — their stale DID cache or inbound-migration policy. Production getServiceAuth mints 60s-TTL lxm tokens. Pre-flight gotcha that cost time: migrated accounts have NO password (MM-306) and the staging account's email was typo'd (MM-308 normalization, MM-309 operator repair ops) — unblocked via requestPasswordReset + token fished from Railway logs (log-only email sender).

Leg (b) took three fixes, each moving the failure one pipeline step (pattern: expect a NEW wall per step when first exercising a reference-PDS seam Custos-to-Custos testing masked):
1. **MM-301** — claim flow cached the W3C DID doc (empty rotationKeys) → migrate button hidden; fix = canonical `GET /{did}/data` fetch everywhere + home-screen cache self-heal (`refresh_did_doc`).
2. **MM-302** — bsky refuses `getServiceAuth(lxm=com.atproto.server.createAccount)` below the *privileged* tier; OAuth `transition:generic` = plain-app-password tier. Fix = outbound-migration source login is a password `createSession` full session (like the claim flow, ADR-0021). Both wallet source logins are now password-based; only the create flow uses OAuth.
3. **MM-304** — Custos `verify_service_auth_jwt` was ES256/P-256-only, but bsky signs service-auth JWTs with the account's secp256k1 `#atproto` key (ES256K). Fix = crypto `verify_did_key_signature` (dual-curve, per-curve low-S) + alg↔key-curve binding in jwt.rs.

**Recurring interop lesson:** bsky signs *everything* (PLC ops, service-auth JWTs) with secp256k1 (`zQ3s…`); any Custos verifier of foreign-account signatures must dispatch both curves. Custos's `require_rpc` is laxer than the reference about which lxm an unprivileged token can mint — [[project-custos-strictness-parity]] / MM-292 family; that laxness masks walls until a bsky source is used.

**Loose ends:** the `.bsky.social` handle is now dangling (bsky no longer actively hosts the account → handle-invalid on the network until a served-domain handle or a migration back). Test-account password `JDZw3if3l!rox1` appears in transcripts — rotate it.

All recorded. Summary of where leg (d) stands:

**The good news inside the failure**: MM-310's fix passed its live trial — the warm-cache `createAccount` on staging (the step that was deterministically doomed two hours ago) verified production's token and resumed the account. The failure moved exactly one step down the pipeline, which has been the run's signature all night.

**The new wall, [MM-316](https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-316/importrepos-first-write-wins-guard-blocks-return-migration-into-a) (Urgent)**: `importRepo` refuses any account that already has a repo root — a guard built for mid-flight retry races, blind to the *completed prior residency* that every round trip creates. The MM-299-resumed leg (b) account still holds its old root, so the 409 is deterministic. The ticket carries a two-tier fix: **idempotent same-root import** (a no-op 200 — sufficient for leg (d), since your repo is byte-identical at rev `3mqdcm57v4u22`) and **replace-on-deactivated via compare-and-swap** (the general different-root return, preserving the anti-race property the old guard provided).

**Nothing needs cleanup**: the resume consumed no claim code and mutated nothing — staging sits exactly as leg (c) left it, and the retry drill is the now-familiar land → staging deploy → same claim code, same build.

Since your other session took MM-310, MM-316 is shaped the same way (single route file + tests, fix design already specced in the ticket) if you want to hand it there — or I can implement it right here; the `import_repo.rs` context is already loaded in this session. Your call.

## Learning Mode Philosophy

Instead of implementing everything yourself, identify opportunities where the user can write 5-10 lines of meaningful code that shapes the solution. Focus on business logic, design choices, and implementation strategies where their input truly matters.

## When to Request User Contributions

Request code contributions for:
- Business logic with multiple valid approaches
- Error handling strategies
- Algorithm implementation choices
- Data structure decisions
- User experience decisions
- Design patterns and architecture choices

## How to Request Contributions

Before requesting code:
1. Create the file with surrounding context
2. Add function signature with clear parameters/return type
3. Include comments explaining the purpose
4. Mark the location with TODO or clear placeholder

When requesting:
- Explain what you've built and WHY this decision matters
- Reference the exact file and prepared location
- Describe trade-offs to consider, constraints, or approaches
- Frame it as valuable input that shapes the feature, not busy work
- Keep requests focused (5-10 lines of code)

## Example Request Pattern

Context: I've set up the authentication middleware. The session timeout behavior is a security vs. UX trade-off - should sessions auto-extend on activity, or have a hard timeout? This affects both security posture and user experience.

Guidance: Consider: auto-extending improves UX but may leave sessions open longer; hard timeouts are more secure but might frustrate active users.

Don't request contributions for:

## Learning Mode Philosophy

Instead of implementing everything yourself, identify opportunities where the user can write 5-10 lines of meaningful code that shapes the solution. Focus on business logic, design choices, and implementation strategies where their input truly matters.

## When to Request User Contributions

Request code contributions for:
- Business logic with multiple valid approaches
- Error handling strategies
- Algorithm implementation choices
- Data structure decisions
- User experience decisions
- Design patterns and architecture choices

## How to Request Contributions

Before requesting code:
1. Create the file with surrounding context
2. Add function signature with clear parameters/return type
3. Include comments explaining the purpose
4. Mark the location with TODO or clear placeholder

When requesting:
- Explain what you've built and WHY this decision matters
- Reference the exact file and prepared location
- Describe trade-offs to consider, constraints, or approaches
- Frame it as valuable input that shapes the feature, not busy work
- Keep requests focused (5-10 lines of code)

## Example Request Pattern

Context: I've set up the authentication middleware. The session timeout behavior is a security vs. UX trade-off - should sessions auto-extend on activity, or have a hard timeout? This affects both security posture and user experience.

Guidance: Consider: auto-extending improves UX but may leave sessions open longer; hard timeouts are more secure but might frustrate active users.

Don't request contributions for:
- Boilerplate or repetitive code
- Obvious implementations with no meaningful choices
- Configuration or setup code
- Simple CRUD operations

Do request contributions when:
- There are meaningful trade-offs to consider
- The decision shapes the feature's behavior
- Multiple valid approaches exist
- The user's domain knowledge would improve the solution

{"id":"MM-241","title":"Validate live bsky.social migration round trip (canonical MM-207 e2e)","description":"## Overview

The canonical end-to-end validation described in the <issue id="4cfdf611-180c-43ee-b3eb-b10a5407e87f" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-207/account-migration-pdspds-full-inbound-outbound-support-epic">MM-207</issue> epic — the only piece of that epic not covered by code + tests. All implementation legs are merged (server XRPC surface, wallet self-signed identity leg, path detection, orchestration, UI, ezpds-as-source e2e test, outbound email); this ticket tracks proving them against the **live network**.

## The round trip (per ADR-0002)

With [bsky.social](<http://bsky.social>) accepting inbound migrations:

1. **(a) Inbound:** import a [bsky.social](<http://bsky.social>) identity into ezpds via the PDS-signed insertion path (email-tokened `signPlcOperation` on [bsky.social](<http://bsky.social>); the op inserts the wallet's device key as `rotationKeys[0]`).
2. **(b) Outbound, self-signed:** migrate that identity *out* of ezpds to a second PDS (staging → production, or vice versa), with the wallet self-signing the PLC op — **this middle leg is the proof of the differentiator**.
3. **(c) Return:** migrate back.

## Tooling notes

* `tools/interop` has `migrate perform` / `migrate verify` for the outbound (self-signed) leg against a live deployment.
* There is currently **no inbound-migration driver** in the interop CLI — the inbound leg is driven from the wallet UI (<issue id="0e291b18-5162-4c8d-9e39-e3b22a031708" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-232/wallet-outbound-migration-ui-obsign">MM-232</issue>) or standard tooling (goat / official client) against ezpds as destination.
* Both ezpds deployments (staging + production) are available as the two PDS endpoints for the middle leg.

## Acceptance

* Each leg's DID audit-log entry on [plc.directory](<http://plc.directory>) shows the expected rotation-key custody at every step.
* Handle/DID/repo resolve to the correct PDS after each leg (`migrate verify` or equivalent).
* Findings (including any interop bugs against [bsky.social](<http://bsky.social>)) recorded here; bugs get their own issues.

Related: <issue id="4cfdf611-180c-43ee-b3eb-b10a5407e87f" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-207/account-migration-pdspds-full-inbound-outbound-support-epic">MM-207</issue> (epic, closed as implementation-complete), ADR-0002.","priority":{"value":0,"name":"No priority"},"url":"https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-241/validate-live-bskysocial-migration-round-trip-canonical-mm-207-e2e","gitBranchName":"malpercio/mm-241-validate-live-bskysocial-migration-round-trip-canonical-mm","createdAt":"2026-07-07T00:14:43.607Z","updatedAt":"2026-07-12T22:13:43.526Z","archivedAt":null,"completedAt":"2026-07-12T22:13:43.498Z","startedAt":"2026-07-08T00:48:17.725Z","canceledAt":null,"dueDate":null,"slaStartedAt":null,"slaMediumRiskAt":null,"slaHighRiskAt":null,"slaBreachesAt":null,"slaType":"all","status":"Done","statusType":"completed","labels":["Wave 7: Hardening"],"attachments":[{"id":"2d1fcd5f-bd6a-4e0e-8009-763fc33f0efe","title":"v0.1 operational proof: metrics endpoint, HTTP integration harness, MM-241 runbook (MM-244)","subtitle":null,"url":"https://github.com/malpercio-dev/ezpds/pull/142"}],"documents":[],"createdBy":"Malpercio","createdById":"5af222b1-08a6-485f-b6e6-26ff3fcff509","assignee":"Malpercio","assigneeId":"5af222b1-08a6-485f-b6e6-26ff3fcff509","project":"ezpds","projectId":"2b0ca2e9-cd15-4ab2-8a55-1efad70eb8a1","team":"Mal's Machinations","teamId":"9278a20f-995f-49ab-b09d-a340fdcaea72"}

# PDS Crate (Custos)

Last verified: 2026-07-05

## Purpose

The PDS is the axum-based web server. It is the sole Imperative Shell in the workspace —
the only crate that touches SQLite, handles HTTP, or manages process-level state. All other
crates (`crypto`, `repo-engine`, `common`) are pure Functional Cores that the PDS calls.

## Module Map

```
src/
  main.rs          — startup: open pool, run migrations, bind server
  telemetry.rs     — OTel tracing-subscriber init (`init_subscriber`) + shutdown-flushing `OtelGuard`; wired by main.rs at startup, dropped after graceful shutdown. `[telemetry] log_format = "json"` switches the stdout fmt layer to one-JSON-object-per-line
  metrics.rs       — OTel meter + Prometheus registry behind `GET /metrics` (see "Metrics" section below): typed `Metrics` handle in AppState, instrument/label name constants (`metrics::names`), the `http_requests_total` middleware, and the `SubscriberGuard` RAII gauge
  app.rs           — AppState definition and construction
  firehose.rs      — persistent subscribeRepos event pipeline (durable sequencer + broadcast fan-out)
  firehose_gc.rs   — periodic `repo_seq` retention sweep (age/count pruning below the live frontier)
  blob_store.rs    — blob storage backend: filesystem I/O, CID computation, MIME-type detection; blobs live at `{data_dir}/blobs/{cid[0:2]}/{cid}`
  blob_gc.rs       — periodic blob GC over per-account ownership rows (`blob_owners`, V039): reconciles each account's MST-referenced blobs into its ownership rows (permanent vs released-with-grace, adopting referenced-but-unowned stored CIDs), then sweeps expired unreferenced rows — the shared physical row + file are deleted only when the last owner is gone
  crawler.rs       — outbound requestCrawl notifier (rate-limited, retrying, fire-and-forget)
  email.rs         — pluggable outbound email sender (`Arc<dyn EmailSender>` in AppState): `LogEmailSender` (default; logs instead of sending — keeps tests/fresh installs offline) + `SmtpEmailSender` (real delivery via `lettre`, rustls). Backs the password-reset / email-confirmation / email-update / PLC-op / account-delete token deliveries. Configured by `[email]` in `pds.toml` / `EZPDS_EMAIL_*`
  rate_limit.rs    — request rate-limiting middleware + shared limiter state (global IP, per-endpoint IP, per-account write points)
  iroh_tunnel.rs   — Iroh QUIC endpoint: NAT-traversing device↔pds tunnel (opt-in)
  record_write.rs  — shared repo write flow + firehose commit emission + post-commit block GC (reuses the firehose diff's `reachable(new)` set as the GC keep-set, so a commit walks repo reachability once, not again per write — see `gc_repo_blocks`)
  account_delete.rs— shared permanent account-deletion transaction (all child tables in FK order — no account-keyed FK cascades exist — plus on-disk reclamation of blob files no other account owns and an `#account` deleted frame), used by deleteAccount and the reaper
  account_reaper.rs— periodic sweep that permanently deletes deactivated accounts past their `deleteAfter` (template: firehose_gc.rs)
  agent_claim_sweep.rs— periodic sweep flipping lapsed pending agent claim attempts to `expired` and recording a `claim_expired` audit event per attempt, in one transaction (template: account_reaper.rs; interval: `[agent_auth] claim_sweep_interval_secs` / `EZPDS_AGENT_CLAIM_SWEEP_INTERVAL_SECS`)
  admin_nonce_sweep.rs— periodic sweep deleting stale `admin_nonces` rows via `db::admin_devices::sweep_stale_nonces` (template: account_reaper.rs; pure storage reclamation — the `(device_id, nonce)` primary key enforces replay rejection, and config validation keeps `nonce_max_age_secs` above the request's full `2 * common::ADMIN_TIMESTAMP_WINDOW_SECS` replay-acceptance span so a swept row can never still be within it; interval: `[admin_devices] nonce_sweep_interval_secs` / `EZPDS_ADMIN_DEVICES_NONCE_SWEEP_INTERVAL_SECS`, retention: `nonce_max_age_secs` / `EZPDS_ADMIN_DEVICES_NONCE_MAX_AGE_SECS`)
  sweep_status.rs  — readable last-run state per periodic sweep (`AppState.sweeps`): each sweep records `{completed_at, swept}` beside its write-only OTel gauge writes so `GET /v1/admin/health` can report it as JSON; shares the sweeps' failure posture (a failed pass records nothing — staleness is the alarm)
  genesis.rs       — shared did:plc genesis-op machinery (verify/validate, DID-doc + CAR builders, plc.directory POST), used by both create_did.rs and create_account_xrpc.rs
  plc_ops.rs       — shared did:plc rotation/update-op machinery for the interop PLC-signing surface: fetch a DID's current PLC state (audit-log GET), render a DID doc from op fields, parse request verificationMethods/services; used by the identity.*PlcOperation routes
  transfer.rs      — shared planned device-transfer accept/complete/cancel workflows composing multi-table transactions; `db/transfers.rs` owns the SQL, this module owns the cross-table ordering (cancel is the operator interruption: flip to terminal `cancelled`, tombstone the accepted device credential, append a `transfer.cancelled` audit event — existing account sessions deliberately untouched)
  handle.rs        — handle validation (structural + domain policy + operator-configurable reserved infrastructure names via `Config::reserved_handles`, default `identitywallet`/`about`), shared by provisioning + handle routes; updateHandle's served-domain branch applies `is_reserved_name(name, &config.reserved_handles)` itself
  identity_resolution.rs— shared handle/DID resolution chain (local handles table → DNS TXT → HTTP well-known) behind resolveHandle/resolveIdentity/refreshIdentity/resolveDid, plus `atproto-proxy` header target resolution with SSRF-guarded endpoint validation for the moderation proxy branch. `resolve_did_document` is cache-first; `resolve_did_document_force_refresh` bypasses the cache, fetches the authoritative doc (plc.directory / did:web), and rewrites the existing cache row (`db::dids::rewrite_did_document`, UPDATE-only) — the `did_documents` cache has no TTL, so this is the only path that un-stales a row. Backs `refreshIdentity` and the migration-`createAccount` verify retry
  dns.rs           — `DnsProvider` (create/delete a handle's DNS records on registration/removal; v0.1 ships no provider, DNS is managed manually) + `TxtResolver` (DNS TXT fallback for resolveHandle; `HickoryTxtResolver` is the production impl)
  well_known.rs    — `WellKnownResolver`: HTTP `.well-known/atproto-did` fallback for resolveHandle (third fallback, after local DB and DNS TXT)
  jwks.rs          — dynamic issuer-key resolution for the auth.md `identity_assertion` flow: `JwksFetcher` (production `HttpJwksFetcher` + injectable mocks) + a TTL `JwksCache` (keyed by `jwks_url`, selects the ID-JAG `kid`), backing `[agent_auth] trusted_issuers[].jwks_url` (the static-PEM trust path never touches it). A per-URL refetch cooldown (`[agent_auth] jwks_refetch_cooldown_secs`, stamped per fetch *attempt*) bounds how often the public agent-auth endpoints can force an outbound fetch via an unverified bogus `kid` (or a failing issuer)
  token.rs         — bearer/device token generation + hashing (pure), shared by the auth guards and session-issuing routes
  code_gen.rs      — random claim-code generation (pure), shared by claim-code + account-creation routes
  uniqueness.rs    — email/handle pre-flight uniqueness DB checks, shared by the account-creation routes
  platform.rs      — device `Platform` enum, shared by the device-registration routes
  read_after_write/— buffered AppView response munge path for read-after-write: merges requester's unindexed records, rev-faithful selection via atproto-repo-rev, fallback ladder, Atproto-Upstream-Lag header
  auth/            — authentication primitives + route guards (HTTP-aware, no DB schema ownership)
  db/              — SQL query functions + migration runner (no business logic)
  routes/          — HTTP handlers, one file per endpoint
```

### `firehose.rs`

The **persistent** event pipeline behind `com.atproto.sync.subscribeRepos`. Holds a durable
monotonic sequencer (backed by the `repo_seq` table, V028) and a Tokio `broadcast` channel;
`AppState.firehose: Arc<Firehose>` is shared by every handler. Each repo commit calls
`record_write::commit_repo_write`, which builds the commit's block diff
(`repo_engine::collect_commit_diff` — one walk of the new root, yielding both the `added` diff
blocks and the `new_reachable` keep-set — + `build_car_from_cids`, run *before* post-commit GC) and
publishes a sequenced `CommitEvent` carrying the DID, rev, `since`, `prevData` (the previous
commit's MST root CID — Sync v1.1's inductive-validation anchor, captured before the write mutates
the repo; `None` for genesis), per-record `RepoOp`s (action + collection/rkey + cid + prev + value;
`prev` is the previous record CID for an update/delete — Sync v1.1's per-op inductive-validation
anchor — `None` for a create), and
the CARv1 diff blocks. The `#commit` wire frame emits the deprecated `blobs` list empty. Backpressure is by design: the bounded
channel never blocks producers — a slow subscriber observes `Lagged` and is expected to disconnect.
All three write paths (`create_record`/`put_record` via `record_write`, `delete_record`,
`apply_writes`) emit exactly one event per commit. (Those same write paths reject a deactivated
account with 403 before committing.) `create_did.rs`'s `promote_account` stages the same kind of
`#commit` event for a new account's *genesis* repo, atomically with the `accounts`/`did_documents`/
`sessions` inserts, so a fresh host self-announces to the relay instead of staying invisible until
its first record write; chained after that genesis `#commit` in the same transaction is a Sync v1.1
`#sync` state assertion (via `PendingCommit::stage_sync`, carrying a single-root CAR of just the
signed commit block), so a relay can anchor to this fresh host's head. It then emits a best-effort
`#account` (active) frame and calls `crawlers.notify()` once that transaction has committed.
A `#sync` frame (`SyncEvent`: DID, rev, and a ≤10 KB commit-block CAR) is the Sync v1.1 head
assertion relays use to auto-repair drift; it is emitted on account genesis (above) and on
`activateAccount` (chained after the `#account` via `PendingAccount::stage_sync` when the account
has a repo — the commit-block CAR is built *before* the transaction, since the single-connection
pool can't serve a block read while the tx holds the connection), and belongs on a future
`importRepo` once that lands. Account-status changes emit a separate
`#account` frame instead of a `#commit`: `activate_account.rs`/`deactivate_account.rs` stage one
via `Firehose::stage_account` (active=false/`deactivated` or active=true) **only on a real status
transition** — a redundant no-op activate/deactivate returns 200 and emits nothing.
`update_subject_status.rs` (`com.atproto.admin.updateSubjectStatus`) stages the same kind of frame
for an admin-driven takedown/clear, but derives `active`/`status` from the account's full
`AccountLifecycle` after the write rather than assuming its own dimension won — clearing a
takedown on a still-suspended account must report `suspended`, not `active`. The `#account` frame
shares the same sequencer so account frames are ordered relative to commits.

**Durability and atomicity.** `Firehose::emit_commit`/`emit_account`/`emit_identity`/`emit_sync`
persist each event to
`repo_seq` (via `db::firehose_seq`) **before** broadcasting it, all under one async `emit_lock`
that keeps broadcast order = `seq` order and the log a dense prefix (a failed insert doesn't
consume a `seq`). The sequencer loads `MAX(seq)` on construction, so `seq` is monotonic across
restarts/redeploys. Those methods remain bare best-effort primitives — used directly by tests,
`emit_identity`'s neighbours (`create_handle.rs`/`delete_handle.rs`/`update_handle.rs`), and
`create_did.rs`'s post-commit `emit_account` call, none of which need atomicity with a specific
transaction; the call sites that do instead acquire `emit_lock` via `Firehose::lock_emit`
(returning an `EmitGuard`) *before* opening their transaction, then call
`EmitGuard::stage_commit`/`stage_account` to insert the `repo_seq` row into that *caller's own*
open transaction. A caller that also needs a chained `#sync` in the same transaction (genesis,
activation) calls `PendingCommit::stage_sync`/`PendingAccount::stage_sync`, which inserts the
`#sync` row at the next `seq` and returns a `PendingWithSync` whose `finish` broadcasts the primary
event then the `#sync`, advancing the counter past both. The staging insert lands in the caller's
open transaction — the same one carrying the repo-root CAS (`record_write::commit_repo_write`,
`create_did.rs`'s genesis promotion) or the account-status UPDATE (`activate_account`/
`deactivate_account`) — and get back a `Pending*` handle that carries the guard forward. Acquiring
the lock before the transaction (rather than inside the staging call) matters on this crate's
single-connection pool: `emit_commit`/
`emit_account`/`emit_identity` already acquire the lock before touching the pool, so a staging
path that instead opened its transaction first and acquired the lock after could deadlock against
one of them (each would hold what the other is waiting for). The caller commits that transaction
and only then calls `Pending*::finish` to advance `last_seq` and broadcast; a failed insert rolls
the whole transaction back (via `?`/`Drop`) rather than landing the state change with a
silently-dropped event, and dropping a `Pending*` without finishing never advances the sequence,
so the seq is retried by the next emit. The one asymmetric drop — a handler future cancelled
(client disconnect) *after* its `tx.commit()` made the staged row durable but before `finish` —
leaves `last_seq` behind the durable log; every insert goes through
`Firehose::insert_at_frontier`, which detects the resulting PRIMARY KEY collision, re-derives the
frontier from the durable `MAX(seq)`, and retries once, so one cancelled request costs one
never-broadcast event (still replayable from the log, like any pre-restart event) instead of
wedging all writes until restart. `subscribe_from(cursor)` snapshots the live receiver and
the sequence frontier `upper` together under
`emit_lock`; the `sync_subscribe_repos` handler then pages the durable log for `(cursor, upper]`
(`events_in_range`, decoded via `decode_stored_event`) and streams live events (`seq > upper`)
after — the two ranges are exactly disjoint, so the replay→live boundary has no gap and no
duplication, and replay now survives a restart (it reads the log, not an in-memory buffer). The
subscriber-facing WebSocket frame encoding lives in the `sync_subscribe_repos` handler.

### `crawler.rs`

Outbound `com.atproto.sync.requestCrawl` notifier. `AppState.crawlers: Arc<CrawlerNotifier>`
is shared by every handler; `record_write::commit_repo_write` calls `crawlers.notify()`
once per commit, right after the firehose event is emitted. `notify` is fire-and-forget: it
selects the crawlers outside their rate-limit window (one notification per crawler per 30s),
then spawns a detached task per crawler that POSTs `{ "hostname": <PDS-host> }` to
`<url>/xrpc/com.atproto.sync.requestCrawl`, retrying with exponential backoff up to 3 times.
All outcomes are logged, never propagated — a commit never blocks on or fails because of a
crawler. Configured via `[crawlers] urls = [...]` (default `["https://bsky.network"]`; empty
disables) or `EZPDS_CRAWLERS`.

### `rate_limit.rs`

Reference-parity request rate limiting. The pure sliding-window algorithm (`MultiWindowLimiter`,
supporting several windows per key with weighted "points") lives in `auth/rate_limit.rs` (Functional
Core); this module is the Imperative Shell that owns the process-level `Mutex`-wrapped limiters and
the Axum middleware. Three families, all off when `[rate_limit] enabled = false` (the test harness
sets this):

1. **Global per-IP** — 1 point/request keyed by client IP (leftmost `X-Forwarded-For`, else the TCP
   peer), default 3000/5min. `com.atproto.sync.getRepo`, `subscribeRepos`, and `_health` are exempt
   so relay backfill/firehose and platform health checks are never throttled.
2. **Per-endpoint per-IP** — tighter caps on `createAccount`/`createSession`/`resetPassword`/
   `updateHandle` (plus the native `/v1/accounts[/mobile]` signup routes), `/v1/transfer/accept`
   (authenticated by a bare 6-char code, so a short-code endpoint belongs here by default), and
   the agent claim-ceremony pair `/agent/identity/claim/confirm` + `/v1/agents/claim-preview`
   (both validate a guessable 6-digit `user_code`; they **share one limiter instance** so
   alternating endpoints can't double the guess budget), keyed by IP.
3. **Per-account write points** — create=3/update=2/delete=1 over an hourly + daily window, charged
   in `record_write::commit_repo_write` (the single choke point for all four repo-write routes),
   keyed by the **authenticated** DID. Keying on the verified DID — not an unverified token subject —
   is deliberate: otherwise anyone could drain a victim's budget.

Rejections return `429` with the standard error envelope plus `RateLimit-Limit`/`-Remaining`/
`-Reset` and `Retry-After`; successful requests carry the `RateLimit-*` headers of the tightest
applicable limiter. All knobs are configurable via `[rate_limit]` in `pds.toml` / `EZPDS_RATE_LIMIT_*`
(a knob of `0` disables that specific limiter).

### `iroh_tunnel.rs`

The Iroh QUIC tunnel — a NAT-traversing endpoint devices dial by node id instead of by a
routable address. Opt-in via `[iroh] enabled` (default off); when enabled, `main.rs` loads the
persistent node identity (`auth::load_or_create_iroh_secret_key`, backed by the `iroh_identity`
table so the node id is stable across restarts), binds the endpoint with the `N0` preset (n0
discovery + relays), and spawns a detached accept loop. `AppState.iroh: Option<Arc<IrohState>>`
holds the bound endpoint and its node-id string; `get_device_pds` advertises that node id.
The accept loop speaks a minimal v0.1 echo protocol on the `ezpds/iroh/0` ALPN — enough to
prove the bidirectional channel and serve as a liveness probe; the real repo-sync / push
protocols register here later. Errors are logged, never propagated (one bad peer never stops
the loop). The endpoint is closed on graceful shutdown, which ends the accept loop.

### `read_after_write/`

**Read-after-write:** Buffered munge path for six munged AppView NSIDs
(`app.bsky.feed.getTimeline`, `getAuthorFeed`, `getPostThread`, `getActorLikes`,
`app.bsky.actor.getProfile`, `getProfiles`). Merges the requester's unindexed records
(fetched from the firehose event log via `get_records_since_rev`) into the AppView's indexed
response. Selects records by comparing the AppView's `atproto-repo-rev` header to the account's
current repo CID (`repo_seq`): records with `indexed_at` timestamps *after* the AppView's rev
are included. The core `pipethrough_munged` handler implements the full fallback ladder:
(1) upstream error → return error unchanged; (2) non-2xx → return buffered original (except
`getPostThread` 400 NotFound, which triggers reconstruction); (3) JSON parse error → return buffered
original; (4) empty LocalRecords → return buffered original with NO lag header; (5) munge/hydration
errors → log and return buffered original (fallback to untouched upstream response). Response buffering
is capped at 10 MiB; oversized responses trigger early bailout. The `Atproto-Upstream-Lag` header
(milliseconds since the oldest merged record's indexed_at) is set only when local.count > 0.
Submodules:

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `mod.rs` | `pipethrough_munged` handler, fallback ladder, buffering cap, response error handling, lag header calculation |
| `munge.rs` | Per-NSID munges `get_timeline`, `get_author_feed`, `get_post_thread`, `get_actor_likes`, `get_profile`, `get_profiles` — injection/overwriting of the requester's records. `// pattern: Mixed (unavoidable)` (the feed/thread munges orchestrate async hydration through `LocalViewer`) |
| `viewer.rs` | `LocalViewer`: hydrates local records as feed items / profile views with author/counts populated via AppView prefetch, renders quote embeds with appview-fetched URIs (falls back to `#viewNotFound` on errors) |
| `types.rs` | `LocalRecords`, `RecordDescript` — structured container for unindexed records bucket by collection |

The munge path shares `service_proxy::proxy_request` extraction with the streaming fast path
(both mint service auth, both buffer request bodies up to MAX_PROXY_BODY, both forward query params).
`mint_service_auth` is `pub(crate)` so `pipethrough_munged` can re-use the JWT minting logic.

**Config:** The AppView is configured via `[appview]` in `pds.toml` (`EZPDS_APPVIEW_URL` env var,
default `https://api.bsky.app`) and `EZPDS_APPVIEW_DID` (default `did:web:api.bsky.app#bsky_appview`).
The optional `EZPDS_APPVIEW_CDN_URL` (default `https://cdn.bsky.app`) overrides the blob CDN
endpoint in blob embed URLs (useful for egress-heavy testing with a local blobstore).

## Metrics

The federation-health instrument set served by `GET /metrics`. Names and label keys are
constants in `metrics::names` — **this table mirrors that module; change them together.**
Counters are constructed *without* the `_total` suffix (the Prometheus exporter appends it;
a unit test in `metrics.rs` pins the rendered names). All instruments record through the
typed `AppState.metrics` handle; when `[telemetry] metrics_enabled = false` the same handle
drops measurements at the SDK boundary, so call sites never branch.

| Rendered name | Type | Labels | Recorded by |
|---|---|---|---|
| `http_requests_total` | counter | `route` (matched template or `unmatched`), `status_class` | `metrics::http_metrics_middleware` (outside the rate limiter → 429s count; inside CORS → preflights don't) |

| `firehose_events_total` | counter | `frame` (`commit`/`account`/`identity`/`sync`) | `Firehose::broadcast` — the single fan-out choke point |
| `firehose_backfill_window_seconds` | gauge | — | `firehose_gc.rs` after each sweep (age of `MIN(sequenced_at)`; 0 when the log is empty) |
| `firehose_gc_swept_total` / `firehose_gc_last_run_timestamp` | counter / gauge | — | `firehose_gc.rs` after each completed pass |
| `blob_gc_swept_total` / `blob_gc_last_run_timestamp` | counter / gauge | — | `blob_gc.rs` after each completed pass (a failed-to-start pass leaves the timestamp stale on purpose — that staleness is the alarm) |
| `account_reaper_swept_total` / `account_reaper_last_run_timestamp` | counter / gauge | — | `account_reaper.rs` after each completed pass |
| `agent_claim_sweep_swept_total` / `agent_claim_sweep_last_run_timestamp` | counter / gauge | — | `agent_claim_sweep.rs` after each completed pass (error early-returns skip the timestamp on purpose — staleness is the alarm) |
| `admin_nonce_sweep_swept_total` / `admin_nonce_sweep_last_run_timestamp` | counter / gauge | — | `admin_nonce_sweep.rs` after each completed pass |
| `relay_crawl_requests_total` | counter | `outcome` (`ok`/`rejected`/`exhausted`) | `crawler.rs` per finished notification |
| `proxy_requests_total` | counter | `upstream` (`appview`/`chat`/`moderation`), `status_class` | `app.rs::xrpc_handler` on both the streaming and munged paths |
| `proxy_upstream_lag_seconds` | histogram | — | `read_after_write/mod.rs`, same conditional value as the `Atproto-Upstream-Lag` header |
| `rate_limit_rejections_total` | counter | `limiter` (`global_ip`/`endpoint_ip`/`account_writes`) | `rate_limit.rs` middleware; `record_write.rs` for write points |
| `migration_imports_total` | counter | `outcome` (`ok`/`error`) | `routes/import_repo.rs` |

Cardinality rule: label values are always drawn from small fixed sets or the route table —
never from request data (raw URIs, rkeys, DIDs, hostnames).

## Hard Rules

**Routes must not import from other routes.**
If two routes share logic, that logic belongs in `auth/` (pure) or `db/` (queries). A route
importing from another route creates hidden coupling and makes it impossible to reason about
a handler in isolation.

**Every `.rs` file with runtime behavior must have a pattern comment.**
Add `// pattern: Functional Core`, `// pattern: Imperative Shell`, or
`// pattern: Mixed (unavoidable)` at the top of any file containing functions or
orchestration logic. Files with only types, constants, or re-exports are exempt.

**`db/` submodules own queries, not transactions.**
Business-logic transactions (multi-table atomic operations) live in the route handler or
a dedicated helper called by the handler — not inside `db/` functions. `db/` functions
accept `&SqlitePool` or `&mut SqliteTransaction`; they never open transactions themselves
unless the operation is inherently single-table.

**Authentication must never be cookie-based; permissive CORS on the public surface depends on it.**
`app.rs` applies `CorsLayer::permissive()` to the public surface (landing, `.well-known`, OAuth,
agent registration, all XRPC, static assets) but deliberately **not** to the admin/provisioning
`/v1/*` surface (same-origin only). Permissive CORS is safe only because every auth path is
Bearer/DPoP/signed-request — never an ambient cookie — so a hostile origin cannot ride a logged-in
user's credentials. If any future auth mechanism becomes cookie-based, the permissive CORS layer
must be tightened (explicit origin allowlist + credentials handling) in the same change.

## Adding a New Route

1. Create `src/routes/<name>.rs` with `// pattern: Imperative Shell` at the top.
2. If the handler needs shared auth logic → add to `auth/` (pure) or use an existing extractor.
3. If the handler needs a new DB query → add to the appropriate `db/` submodule.
4. Register in `src/app.rs` router.
5. Add a `.bru` file in `bruno/` (see root CLAUDE.md).

## Adding a New DB Query

1. Identify the owning entity (`accounts`, `oauth`, etc.).
2. Add the function to the matching `db/<entity>.rs` file.
3. If no matching file exists, create one with `// pattern: Imperative Shell`.
4. Export the function and any new data struct via `db/mod.rs` (`pub mod <entity>;`).

MM-241 = validate a live bsky.social migration round trip with the wallet.

**Status (2026-07-12):** leg (r) (sim rehearsal staging→production) PASSED; **leg (b) (on-device bsky.social → ezpds-staging) PASSED**; **Custos→Custos live hop (staging → production/obsign.org) PASSED same day, zero new walls** — lossless (same rev both sides), staging cleanly deactivated. Test account `malpercio-obsign.bsky.social` / `did:plc:u7j7xdhvkwx3xlf6xjkbpdn7` now lives on PRODUCTION, device key still rotationKeys[0] through three PLC ops. **Leg letters per the runbook** (`docs/validation/2026-07-07-mm-241-live-migration.md` — the permanent record; operator handle "mal"): (a) claim ✓, (r) sim rehearsal ✓, (b) bsky→staging ✓, (c) staging→production ✓ — **remaining: leg (d) = production → STAGING** (round-trip closure; NOT a return to bsky). **Leg (d) blockers, in discovery order:** MM-310 (fossil DID-doc cache; FIXED + confirmed live on staging 2026-07-12 — the warm-cache createAccount passed) → **MM-316 (current blocker): `importRepo` is first-write-wins (409 "account already has a repo"), and the MM-299-resumed leg (b) staging account still carries its old repo root — a completed prior residency was never in the guard's picture; any round trip trips it.** Fix tiers: idempotent same-root import (alone unblocks leg (d) — the incoming repo is byte-identical, same rev) + replace-on-deactivated via CAS. Leg (d) attempt 1 is cleanly retryable (resume consumed no claim code). Sequence: land MM-316 → staging deploy → retry leg (d). Runbook's execution-record table still needs legs (b)/(c) rows appended (evidence in MM-241 comments).

Extra-curricular bsky-return probing (not a required leg): bsky's entryway auth-gates reserveSigningKey, phone-gates createAccount, and rejected a PROVABLY VALID production ES256 service token (verified perfect against a local Custos impersonating did:web:bsky.social) — their stale DID cache or inbound-migration policy. Production getServiceAuth mints 60s-TTL lxm tokens. Pre-flight gotcha that cost time: migrated accounts have NO password (MM-306) and the staging account's email was typo'd (MM-308 normalization, MM-309 operator repair ops) — unblocked via requestPasswordReset + token fished from Railway logs (log-only email sender).

Leg (b) took three fixes, each moving the failure one pipeline step (pattern: expect a NEW wall per step when first exercising a reference-PDS seam Custos-to-Custos testing masked):
1. **MM-301** — claim flow cached the W3C DID doc (empty rotationKeys) → migrate button hidden; fix = canonical `GET /{did}/data` fetch everywhere + home-screen cache self-heal (`refresh_did_doc`).
2. **MM-302** — bsky refuses `getServiceAuth(lxm=com.atproto.server.createAccount)` below the *privileged* tier; OAuth `transition:generic` = plain-app-password tier. Fix = outbound-migration source login is a password `createSession` full session (like the claim flow, ADR-0021). Both wallet source logins are now password-based; only the create flow uses OAuth.
3. **MM-304** — Custos `verify_service_auth_jwt` was ES256/P-256-only, but bsky signs service-auth JWTs with the account's secp256k1 `#atproto` key (ES256K). Fix = crypto `verify_did_key_signature` (dual-curve, per-curve low-S) + alg↔key-curve binding in jwt.rs.

**Recurring interop lesson:** bsky signs *everything* (PLC ops, service-auth JWTs) with secp256k1 (`zQ3s…`); any Custos verifier of foreign-account signatures must dispatch both curves. Custos's `require_rpc` is laxer than the reference about which lxm an unprivileged token can mint — [[project-custos-strictness-parity]] / MM-292 family; that laxness masks walls until a bsky source is used.

**Loose ends:** the `.bsky.social` handle is now dangling (bsky no longer actively hosts the account → handle-invalid on the network until a served-domain handle or a migration back). Test-account password `JDZw3if3l!rox1` appears in transcripts — rotate it.

content.text:
🏁 **MM-241 is Done. The round trip is closed, verified, and permanently recorded.**

The final state of the board:

- **The proof**: `did:plc:u7j7xdhvkwx3xlf6xjkbpdn7` left bsky.social, lived on two independent Custos deployments, and returned home to staging — **four PLC operations, every one self-signed by the key in your phone's Secure Enclave, `rotationKeys[0]` never changing hands**, and the repo at the identical rev in all four residencies. No server ever held the root of the identity, and no server could have vetoed a single hop. That's ADR-0002's differentiator demonstrated on the live network, end to end.
- **The record**: [execution record](docs/validation/2026-07-07-mm-241-live-migration.md) complete for all five legs (commit `13744865`), status header flipped to COMPLETE, [MM-241](https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-241/validate-live-bskysocial-migration-round-trip-canonical-mm-207-e2e) closed with the link per the runbook's own criterion.
- **The harvest**: ten defects found, fixed, deployed, and validated *by the leg that found them* — plus nine follow-on design/UX tickets (sovereign passwordless login, handle-change flow, operator repair ops, email normalization, the login papercuts) and the bsky inbound-posture finding, which reads like the product's thesis statement rendered as error codes: leaving bsky.social works; returning is not currently accepted.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
The run's most valuable output may be the *pattern*, not any single fix: every leg failed exactly one pipeline step past the previous fix — auth tier, token curve, cache freshness, import semantics. That's what "the seam was never exercised" looks like empirically, and it's why the runbook's "expect this" warning and stop-fix-retry discipline (rather than papering over a failed check) paid off: each wall became a deployed fix validated by a live retry the same night, instead of a latent bug for the first real user.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

Loose threads for daylight, none urgent: the runbook's optional post-run `just interop suite --no-interact` against staging; MM-316's CAS tier wants an interop test with a genuinely diverged repo; the test account's handle remains network-dangling until it gets a served-domain handle (MM-305's flow, when it exists); and production still runs pre-MM-310/316 code until the next release train — worth cutting v0.4.6 before any migration touches production as a *destination* again.

Tonight: three fixes shipped from this session, two more landed from your parallel sessions, four live legs passed, and the epic-closing e2e that had been open since the migration epic began — done. Go enjoy the victory, mal. 🎉

content.content:
## Capability coverage vs. a daily-driver Bluesky PDS

Every `com.atproto.*` route a daily driver needs is implemented: server sessions,
createAccount/describeServer, app passwords, email/account management, repo CRUD + applyWrites
+ uploadBlob + importRepo + listMissingBlobs, the full sync surface incl. Sync v1.1 (`#sync`
frames, `prevData`, per-op `prev`) and `subscribeRepos`, identity (resolve/updateHandle/PLC-op
signing), service proxying to the AppView with read-after-write munging, chat proxy, the full
atproto OAuth provider stack (PAR, DPoP, rotating refresh, revoke, client-metadata resolution,
granular scopes), preferences, invite/signup, and moderation/admin.

**The gaps are validation, not features:**
1. The **live migration round trip** (bsky.social → ezpds and the credible-exit leg, MM-241)
   has never been executed — the runbook exists with a blank execution record. This is the exact
   path a real account takes. Do not move a real account before it passes.
2. **First real OAuth login by the official Bluesky app** is implemented but unproven — the
   interop suite and HTTP tests authenticate with `createSession` passwords, never OAuth/DPoP.
3. **`atproto-proxy` header is honored only for `com.atproto.moderation.*`**, not `app.bsky.*`,
   so `app.bsky.video.*` (routed by the official app with that header) will not reach the video
   service — **posting video from the official app likely fails**. The resolution machinery
   already exists in the moderation branch; generalizing it is the fix.
4. **Operational config, not code:** the default email sender only logs — password reset,
   PLC-op, email-confirm and account-delete tokens go nowhere until `[email] provider = "smtp"`
   is set.

Proven against the live network (interop suite, staging): account provisioning, identity
triple-agreement, repo CRUD with CID match, live firehose observation, CAR export consistency,
PDS→AppView proxy auth, real social interactions, full account lifecycle incl. reaper purge.

---

## Refactoring opportunities (for contributor onboarding)

1. **Extract the shared record-write preamble.** `delete_record.rs` and `apply_writes.rs`
   duplicate `record_write.rs`'s entire gather phase (DID resolution, auth/scope, lifecycle 403,
   root load, signer load) verbatim — three copies of the lifecycle-guard reasoning is where the
   next drift bug lands.
2. **Unify blob ownership with the block model** (also fixes H2): a `blob_owners` table would
   make the two content-addressed stores one teachable pattern.
3. **Split the largest modules:** `routes/oauth_token.rs` (~3.1k lines; three grant handlers +
   claim polling), `firehose.rs` (~2.5k; sequencer + staging state machine + stored-event codec —
   the codec is a clean Functional Core extraction), `read_after_write/mod.rs`, `create_did.rs`,
   `db/accounts.rs`.
4. **Move refresh-token rotation SQL into `db/refresh_tokens.rs`** so the table's write-side
   invariants (the guard from fix #7) live next to its reads, per the crate's "queries in db/"
   rule (`db/transfers.rs` already takes `&mut SqliteTransaction`).
5. **One generic sweeper scaffold** for `account_reaper.rs`/`blob_gc.rs`/`firehose_gc.rs` — they
   hand-roll the identical spawn/interval/stats/metrics skeleton (~120 duplicated lines).

5:v0.1 Draft — March 2026
13:The architecture defined two milestones (v0.1, v1.0). The mobile spec defined four (v0.1, v0.2, v1.0, v2.0+). The mobile spec is canonical. This document reconciles both into a single timeline.
17:The architecture was written before the mobile-first strategy existed. Its two milestones assumed a desktop-only product. The mobile spec introduced a PDS-as-full-PDS phase that precedes any desktop involvement. The four-phase model reflects the actual build order:
19:1. **v0.1** — PDS is a full PDS. User creates identity from phone, logs into Bluesky.
28:| v0.1 | 3–4 months | 3–4 months |
39:### 2.1 v0.1 — Mobile-Only PDS
72:| Local filesystem storage | Default for v0.1 (S3 optional via config) | blob spec §3 |
170:#### Not in v0.1
208:#### Unchanged from v0.1
273:How each document's milestones map to the unified phases:
277:| **v0.1** | v0.1 (technical preview) | iOS v0.1 (identity wallet) | Core endpoints | v0.1 (planned swap) | v0.1 (basic OAuth) | v0.1 (basic blobs) |
279:| **v1.0** | v1.0 (public launch) | iOS v1.0 (recovery) | Full API + milestones | v1.0 (full recovery) | v1.0 (production) | v1.0 (production) |
284:The architecture document has no v0.2 milestone. It needs a "Phase 1: Desktop Enrollment" between its technical preview and public launch. The architecture's v0.1 scope includes some items that belong in v0.2 (device pairing, desktop promotion).
288:The provisioning API has no milestone tags at all. Every endpoint group needs a phase assignment. The 17 endpoints from the mobile and migration specs need to be integrated and tagged.
297:v0.1 Critical Path:

{"issues":[{"id":"MM-317","title":"Admin-companion break-glass transport: HTTP over the iroh tunnel","description":"## Overview

Pilot HTTP-over-iroh on the **admin-companion only**, as a break-glass transport: the operator console stays reachable when DNS is broken, the relay's cert expired, or the HTTPS edge is misconfigured — exactly the moments an operator needs the console. This is the one bounded, honest slice of "apps talk to Custos over iroh"; general API tunneling for both apps was assessed and rejected (public HTTPS must exist anyway for federation … (truncated, use `get_issue` for full description)","priority":{"value":0,"name":"No priority"},"url":"https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-317/admin-companion-break-glass-transport-http-over-the-iroh-tunnel","gitBranchName":"malpercio/mm-317-admin-companion-break-glass-transport-http-over-the-iroh","createdAt":"2026-07-12T21:23:23.566Z","updatedAt":"2026-07-12T21:23:23.566Z","archivedAt":null,"completedAt":null,"startedAt":null,"canceledAt":null,"dueDate":null,"slaStartedAt":null,"slaMediumRiskAt":null,"slaHighRiskAt":null,"slaBreachesAt":null,"slaType":"all","status":"Backlog","statusType":"backlog","labels":["Wave 7: Hardening"],"createdBy":"Malpercio","createdById":"5af222b1-08a6-485f-b6e6-26ff3fcff509","project":"ezpds","projectId":"2b0ca2e9-cd15-4ab2-8a55-1efad70eb8a1","team":"Mal's Machinations","teamId":"9278a20f-995f-49ab-b09d-a340fdcaea72"},{"id":"MM-315","title":"Migration source login prefills the DID instead of the handle","description":"## Problem (user-observed, on device, <issue id="10c8aa2a-f2fe-433f-9ba4-fed81b554e7a" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-241/validate-live-bskysocial-migration-round-trip-canonical-mm-207-e2e">MM-241</issue> legs (b)/(c))

The outbound-migration source-login screen prefills the identifier field with the **DID** (`did:plc:…`) rather than the handle — technically valid (createSession accepts DIDs) but strange as a user: you expect to see… (truncated, use `get_issue` for full description)","priority":{"value":4,"name":"Low"},"url":"https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-315/migration-source-login-prefills-the-did-instead-of-the-handle","gitBranchName":"malpercio/mm-315-migration-source-login-prefills-the-did-instead-of-the","createdAt":"2026-07-12T20:50:11.592Z","updatedAt":"2026-07-12T20:50:11.592Z","archivedAt":null,"completedAt":null,"startedAt":null,"canceledAt":null,"dueDate":null,"slaStartedAt":null,"slaMediumRiskAt":null,"slaHighRiskAt":null,"slaBreachesAt":null,"slaType":"all","status":"Backlog","statusType":"backlog","labels":[],"createdBy":"Malpercio","createdById":"5af222b1-08a6-485f-b6e6-26ff3fcff509","project":"ezpds","projectId":"2b0ca2e9-cd15-4ab2-8a55-1efad70eb8a1","team":"Mal's Machinations","teamId":"9278a20f-995f-49ab-b09d-a340fdcaea72"},{"id":"MM-314","title":"Create-flow OAuth login UX — no username autofill (login_hint never passed) and iOS auto-capitalization breaks sign-in","description":"## Problem (user-observed, on device)

During the create flow's first OAuth (the `authenticating` step after handle registration), the in-app authorize page:

1. **Doesn't prefill the username** — even though the wallet literally just registered the handle two screens earlier.
2. **iOS auto-capitalizes the first letter** of the identifier, and the login then fails — annoying and mysterious to a user (the failure gives no hint that case was the p… (truncated, use `get_issue` for full description)","priority":{"value":3,"name":"Medium"},"url":"https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-314/create-flow-oauth-login-ux-no-username-autofill-login-hint-never","gitBranchName":"malpercio/mm-314-create-flow-oauth-login-ux-no-username-autofill-login_hint","createdAt":"2026-07-12T20:50:07.325Z","updatedAt":"2026-07-12T20:50:07.325Z","archivedAt":null,"completedAt":null,"startedAt":null,"canceledAt":null,"dueDate":null,"slaStartedAt":null,"slaMediumRiskAt":null,"slaHighRiskAt":null,"slaBreachesAt":null,"slaType":"all","status":"Backlog","statusType":"backlog","labels":[],"createdBy":"Malpercio","createdById":"5af222b1-08a6-485f-b6e6-26ff3fcff509","project":"ezpds","projectId":"2b0ca2e9-cd15-4ab2-8a55-1efad70eb8a1","team":"Mal's Machinations","teamId":"9278a20f-995f-49ab-b09d-a340fdcaea72"},{"id":"MM-308","title":"Normalize account emails — Custos matches byte-exact where the reference PDS lowercases","description":"## Problem

Account emails are stored verbatim and every lookup is byte-exact (`db::accounts::resolve_by_email`: `WHERE a.email = ?`; same for the uniqueness preflight in `uniqueness.rs` and the `confirmEmail`/`updateEmail` match). The reference PDS lowercases emails on store and lookup.
